Outcomes/Publications: This award allowed us to asses the role of PKR1 and PKR2 in the regulation of food intake. We demonstrated, using new mouse models, that, unlike previously thought, the anorexigenic effect of PK2 was mediated through PKR2 rather than PKR1. Additionally, we established that the site of action of PK2 was not the hypothalamus but rather the amygdala. This work identifies PKR2 in the amygdala, and more specifically the central nucleus of the amygdala, as an important regulator of the energy homeostasis machinery and a new promising target for the treatment of obesity.    https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9860486 Activation of amygdala prokineticin receptor 2 neurons drives the anorexigenic activity of the neuropeptide PK2.
